sentences.text: The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.295 of 2023, registered under Sections 420, 406 I.P.C. at Police Station- Vrindavan, District- Mathura with a prayer to enlarge her on anticipatory bail.
5. As per prosecution story, the informant and family members of the applicant were having cordial family relationship with each other for the last 30-35 years.
Subsequent to it, the applicant and other members of the family are stated to have agreed to sell their house for a consideration of Rs.95,00,000/- in the year 2019.
Pursuant to it, an amount of Rs.11,00,000/- is stated to have been given in cash to the applicant and co-accused person Mamta Sharma on 5.4.2019 by the informant.
Subsequent to it, Rs.35,00,000/- are stated to have been given through cheque and other transactions to other co-accused persons.
The applicant and other members of the family are subsequently stated to have refused to execute the sale-deed and have usurped the said amount.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that she has been falsely implicated in this case.
The case of civil in nature has been converted into criminal one by the informant.
The applicant and her husband had fallen apart, as such family dispute is going on between them.
The applicant resides at her maternal home and not at the said house, although her Aadhar Card reveals her address to be that of co-accused persons, which pertains to the house in question.
It is further stated that the applicant has simply been made an accused on the basis of the said relationship with her estranged husband Gopeshwar Sharan.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that the criminal history of one case assigned to the applicant stands explained as the proceedings in the said case have been stayed by this Court vide order dated 20.11.2020 passed in Application U/s 482 No.16705 of 2020.

In support of this submission, learned counsel has placed much reliance upon the judgment of Prabhakar Tewari Vs.
State of U.P. and another, 2020 (11) SCC 648, wherein the Supreme Court has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail, if otherwise his case of bail is made out.
8.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that there is no proof of any handing over of money to the applicant.
The allegations of handing over the money in cash are vague.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against her.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The applicant has apprehension of her arrest.

Learned counsel has stated that the applicant undertakes that she has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application on the ground that the affidavit is false as the applicant has shown the address of house in question herein, which has been subsequently sold by the applicant and other co-accused persons on 21.9.2020.

It is also argued that the applicant and other co-accused persons had filed separate criminal writ petitions before this Court and were granted interim protection on the ground that they are ready to get the matter settled at Mediation Centre of this Court, but Smt Krishna Alias Kripa Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64183143/

sentences.text: despite taking time twice, they had not deposited single penny for initiating the mediation proceedings.
As such, the applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration that applicant is living separately to her husband Gopeshwar Sharan, who alongwith co-accused person Mamta Sharma is the main accused person, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020)
5 SCC 1".

5 SCC 1"
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Supreme Court.
11. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
12. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.
